entry.title: Dan Abramov Uses AI Agents to Obtain a Lean Proof of Conway's Conjecture
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | overreacted.io | hacker news

Using a multi-agent AI workflow, Dan Abramov has obtained a Lean formalization of John Conway's refinement conjecture regarding omnific integers. The methodology involved a specialized system of LLM agents—including roles for project management, mathematical research, and skepticism—designed to move past AI hallucinations toward structured mathematical proofs.

The resulting proof has passed mechanical verification via the Palomar registry and has undergone initial review by experts in the field. This approach highlights a potential pathway for agentic reasoning systems to solve and formalize complex problems within the surreal number system.

entry.title: Leopardus tilcayo Identified as New Cat Species in Bolivia
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | nationalgeographic.com | source | hacker news

Researchers have identified a new species of wild cat, Leopardus tilcayo, in the Yungas forest of Bolivia. The findings, published in the journal Current Biology, mark the first new cat species discovered in more than 100 years. Genomic analysis indicates that the feline diverged from the Leopardus tigrinus lineage approximately 1.4 million years ago.

This discovery demonstrates how genomic analysis can reveal species that are visually indistinguishable, a method researchers hope to use to find more hidden cat species worldwide. These findings have significant conservation implications, as the identification of distinct species often necessitates more targeted and urgent protection strategies for localized populations.

entry.title: The Scale and Cultural Significance of U.S. Self-Storage Facilities
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | newyorker.com | hacker news

The United States holds approximately 90 percent of the world's self-storage capacity, a sector generating over $40 billion in annual revenue. Driven by life events such as death, divorce, and downsizing, the industry's total number of locations exceeds the combined count of Starbucks, McDonald's, Walmart, Home Depot, Domino's, Dunkin', and Costco.

The market has evolved from small-scale local operations into a major institutional asset class. This landscape is served by large national chains, such as Public Storage and Extra Space Storage, as well as emerging digital marketplace models like Neighbor.

entry.title: Terence Tao's Response to the Fields Medalists' AI Declaration
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | gowers.wordpress.com | source | hacker news

A joint declaration by 25 Fields Medalists warns that the rise of AI in mathematics could prioritize rapid problem-solving over the conceptual understanding required for mathematical discovery. Terence Tao declined to sign the letter, arguing instead that mathematicians follow a spectrum of motivation between solving problems and gaining insight.

Tao acknowledges the challenge of the mathematical community's ability to absorb a potential influx of AI-generated results. However, he suggests that progress can be sustained if researchers use AI as a tool for active learning and guided discovery rather than as a replacement for human effort.

This connectome details the synaptic connections of more than 166,000 neurons, enabling researchers to conduct high-resolution comparisons of neural structures between sexes.

The digital brain has sparked social media trends where modders simulate neural activity in virtual environments like Minecraft and Doom. In a scientific context, the dataset is intended to facilitate research into motor control, sensory systems, and the fundamental mechanisms of neurobiology.

entry.title: Visual Preference Surveys Suggest Widespread Public Preference for Traditional Architecture
entry.content:

Visual preference surveys conducted in several countries, including the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, and Chile, consistently indicate that a majority of the public prefers traditional architectural styles over modernist designs. These studies often show support for traditional facades and human-scaled, walkable urbanism in the range of 60% to 85%, suggesting a broad public preference for certain aesthetic and structural patterns over unornamented modernism.

Research also highlights a notable divergence between the aesthetic tastes of architectural professionals and those of the general population. Furthermore, findings suggest that these preferences for traditional architecture are remarkably consistent across different demographics, remaining largely unaffected by age, gender, nationality, or political affiliation.

entry.title: Map Projection Transitions from Equal-Area to Mercator on Zoom
entry.content:
Lobsters Top | benjoffe.com | discussion

A mathematical formula enables interactive maps to maintain an equal-area view at a global scale while transitioning seamlessly to a conformal Mercator projection as users zoom. This method uses a closed-form function, `atanh(sin(lat) * a) / a`, where a variable parameter interpolates between equal-area and conformal cylindrical states.

This method offers an alternative to existing projections like Equal Earth, which often require complex iterative math and can cause significant visual distortion in high-latitude regions. The design also facilitates "compromise" cylindrical projections that optimize screen space by reducing the area dedicated to the poles.

entry.title: The Discovery and History of Papua New Guinea's Highland Tribes
entry.content:
Hacker News Best | notnottalmud.substack.com | hacker news

In 1930, Australian explorers unexpectedly discovered massive, isolated populations living in the highlands of Papua New Guinea. These tribes had remained functionally cut off from the rest of the world for millennia, developing independent agricultural techniques and unique social organizations.

Western contact triggered profound cultural and economic shifts, such as the adoption of "big man" leadership models and economic hyperinflation caused by the mass introduction of shell-based currency. These historical encounters are documented in the book *First Contact: New Guinea's Highlanders Encounter the Outside World*.
